::: {#def-separability .theorem}
## Separability

An exposure mapping $g_{ik}$ is separable if it can be written as unit $i$’s own value for each preceding covariate, alongside one summary per covariate:

$$
g_{ik}(\mathbf{X}_1,\dots,\mathbf{X}_{k-1})=\Big[\underbrace{X_{1i},\dots,X_{k-1,i}}_{\in\,\mathbb{R}^{k-1}},\ \underbrace{g_{1i}(\mathbf{X}_1),\dots,g_{k-1,i}(\mathbf{X}_{k-1})}_{\text{each}\,\in\,\mathbb{R}}\Big]^T,
$$

where $X_{ti}\in\mathscr{O}_i$ is unit $i$’s own entry of covariate $\mathbf{X}_t$, and each $g_{ti}:\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{X}_t)\to\mathbb{R}$, called a component function of $g_{ik}$, summarizes covariate $\mathbf{X}_t$ on a network graph (C.20). The value $g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}_t)$ is the network value of unit $i$ for $\mathbf{X}_t$. A structural equation is separable if its exposure mapping is.
:::
